EXTRA TRAINING

This blog post assumes the following updates are applied to the Trained trait from WFRP page 342-343. Of note, look to Broken, which was never supposed to imply the Bestial trait was ignored completely.

Broken: The animal has been domesticated. Now tame, it gains +2d10 Fel, even if it has the Bestial trait. Further, it can now learn more Trained traits (see WFRP page 199).

Calm*: The animal can attempt a Challenging (+0) Cool Test to ignore the effects of the Skittish Creature Trait. It gains a bonus of +10 to this Test for each point it has in Calm. It can have a maximum of WPB rating in this trait.

Drive: The animal is trained to pull a coach, cart, plough, buggy, or similar. The animal can pull up to its own body weight for TB hours without needing to make an Endurance Test. The animal can also pull up to twice its body weight for short hauls of TB minutes. The animal's gains a bonus of +1 TB to do this for each point it has in Drive. It can have a maximum of WPB rating in this trait.

Fetch: The animal is trained to spot and retrieve an object or prey undamaged.

Pack: The animal is trained to carry great weights on its back. It can carry its Strength rating in Encumbrance points upon its back for each point it has in Pack. This limit is doubled for each step in the Size trait to the creature has above Large. It can have a maximum of TB rating in this trait.

Pointer: The animal is trained to spot birds and 'point' to them by freezing and aiming their muzzle towards the game.

Magical: The animal is trained to accept a spellcaster as a rider. Without this Trained trait, the animal typically shies from spellcasters.

War: The animal is trained to carry a rider into the hell of war. It can use its Rider’s WP instead of its own for all appropriate Tests

*Updated

 

TRAITS

Amble

The creature has a smooth gait, making it more comfortable to ride over long distances. Add +Amble hours to any length of time a rider can comfortably ride. Further, reduce the Combat Difficulty for Shooting From Horseback by 1 step.*

*: Amble references rules I use where you can't ride a horse for longer than TB hours a day without picking up some Fatigue Conditions, depending upon the results of an Endurance Test. Further, Shooting From Horseback is a penalty of at least –20, depending upon the circumstances. Riders with the Trick Riding Talent reduce this difficulty by 1 step.

Fine

This repurposes the Item Fine Quality for animals. For animals the Fine Trait represents a pedigree. Mongrels cannot purchase the Fine Quality to represent breeding, but it could be purchased to show a dog with a particularly pretty face or similar.

If a Player wants to buy any special breed beyond the generic versions, at least 1 instance of Fine should be bought to show it's a purebred animal accessing the special rules.

For each Fine Trait the animal has, its price is doubled and its @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.JournalEntry.sLomXnc8R8518cWN.JournalEntryPage.mSfQGLILlnIVr27i]{Availability} is one step less.

A typical Telland actually starts at 7GC (the base cost of 3GC 10/– is doubled because of the Fine Quality).

The more Fine Traits purchased, the stronger the bloodline of the animal, and the more impressive it appears. This brings no advantages beyond bragging rights and high returns if the animal is ever sold.

NOTE: Insisting special breeds have the Fine quality is not a firm rule, as you may wish to keep costs low at some points; it's more of a guideline that you should most always follow.

Sure-Feet

The creature can instinctually find its footing, even when it has a rider on its back. The creature automatically passes all Tests concerning uncertain footing caused by such things as screes, rocky trails, heavy undergrowth, and similar.

Note: None of the creatures in the WFRP rulebook should have either of these two traits, but they could be used as an Optional wherever you feel it fits.

Swimmer

Start with Swim Skill +10

Ugly

This repurposes the Item Ugly Flaw for animals. Taking the Ugly Trait for your pet shows it's particularly ill-favoured in appearance, which may come with penalties in some situations.

Ugly animals attract negative attention, and related Fellowship Tests might even suffer a –10 penalty.

Each Ugly Trait the animal has, halves the listed price and improves @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.JournalEntry.sLomXnc8R8518cWN.JournalEntryPage.mSfQGLILlnIVr27i]{Availability} by one step. 

Note: Exotic items do not have their Availability modified by being Flawed — they are always difficult to find, even shoddy examples.

NEW TRAITS (mine)

Keen Senses (Sense)

One of the creatures primary five senses is highly developed, or possesses a different sense allowing them to spot what others miss. This normally increases its breadth, range or detail. They may take Perception Tests to detect things that are normally imperceptible with the associated sense, as dictated by the GM and may add SL equal to their Initiative Bonus to all Perception (sense) Tests.
Includes the 5 senses: Sight, Smell, Hearing, Touch, Taste. Electroception for some creatures. Magnetoception is covered by the Wayfinder Trait.

Note 1: Keen senses was designed to fix the fact that animals are famous for their keen senses and yet in general have low initative and so there perception is poor compared to humans. In reality animals tend to rely on a few very developed senses and the others often poorer than ours and sometimes even absent. Hence this trait improves specific senses. Which also makes it more interesting thematically. You probably won't get past a guard dogs due to it's sense of smell or hearing however it's unlikely to be too fussy about drugged dog food if you can disguise the smell.

Note 2: I haven't altered Andy's animals to have these traits. However if you wish to my suggestions are
Dogs: Keen Senses (Smell), Keen Senses (Hearing).

Dogs’ sense of smell is immeasurably better than that of humans. Dogs possess an acute sense of hearing. The eyesight of a dog is not as keen as its sense of smell, and it is generally thought that dogs have poor colour perception.Labrador Retrievers, which are a breed commonly used as seeing-eye dogs for humans, have better eyesight that is closer to ours. The dog’s sense of taste is poor compared with that of humans. If forced to live on their own, dogs will eat almost anything without much discrimination.

Horses: Keen Senses (Hearing), Keen Senses (Smell), Keen Senses (Touch)

A horse’s hearing is much keener than ours. Horses’ ears can rotate about 180 degrees feature allows horses to focus on the direction from which the sound is coming, isolate it, and run the other way. The horse’s range of smell is more acute than that of humans but less sensitive than that of dogs. Touch is one of the main senses of horse-rider communication. Horses’ tactile sensation, or touch, is extremely acute. Their entire body is as sensitive as our fingertips. They can feel a fly on a single hair. Horses have poor colour vision. 

Cats: Keen Senses (Hearing), Keen Senses (Smell), Keen Senses (Touch)

Hearing and smell, and their sense of touch is enhanced by long whiskers that protrude from their heads and bodies. Cats have acute night sight but it's worse than ours during the day generally and there sense of taste is poor for sweet.

Wayfinder

The creature has an instinctual ability through magical or natural senses, such as magnetic fields, reading signs or detecting the winds of magic (from the polar gates), to find their way accurately even without maps or instruments. They add SL equal to their Initiative Bonus to all Navigation Tests.

Survival Sense

The creature has an instinctual ability, to survive in the wild. Start with Outdoor Survival Skill +25.

Notes: Survival sense is designed for animals with an intelligence in the 5-15 range. Which brings them equal to humans or above.
